LESSON: WRITING 3.3.1 SEQUENCING IDEAS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: when using a vehicle) on the theme, 1. How can you ensure your ideas flow in communication?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify connectors in texts for effective communication
2. use connectors to sequence ideas logically in a paragraph for comprehension

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Writing 3.3.1 Sequencing Ideas makes your writing clear so others can read it easily.

• Look at the model your teacher shows. Notice shape, order, and spacing.

• Practise slowly first, then build neat speed.

• Check your work: Did you spell carefully? Did you use correct marks?

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Copy three model sentences neatly, leaving finger spaces between words.

Example 2: Spell five lesson words aloud, then write them without looking.

Example 3: Fix this sentence by adding capital letters and a full stop: “amina went to kisumu”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Write five neat sentences about your school using words from this topic.
2. Exchange books with a friend and check spelling or punctuation together.
3. Rewrite one messy sentence so it is clear and correct.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Complete a short guided paragraph in your exercise book.
2. List eight words from this topic and practise spelling them with a parent.
3. Write a short note to a friend using correct punctuation.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. List connectors on charts for display,
2. Use connectors to write two paragraphs (on safe practices when using a vehicle) on the theme, 1. How can you ensure your ideas flow in communication? 2. Why do we use connectors in writing? 18
3. Read the paragraphs on the theme in class for peer review,
4. Learning to learn: This is enhanced as the learner interacts with content when searching for various connectors used in writing.
5. Critical thinking and Problem solving: This is enhanced as the learner follows simple instructions to connect sentence strips to form a paragraph using appropriate connectors. Values:

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when using a vehicle) on the theme, 1. How can you ensure your ideas flow in communication?
2. Why do we use connectors in writing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Neat writing helps the reader.
2. Check spelling and punctuation before you finish.
3. Practice a little every day.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
